verdict.summary: Creating and testing your own Klaviyo OAuth app with your own account is quick, and you can share the installation URL with test customers without review. Listing the app in the Klaviyo marketplace needs 5 real customer installs with live API activity, a security assessment, and a review that Klaviyo may decline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1 hour for setup and your own test; several days to weeks of work to collect customer installs and complete listing forms (estimate, not documented)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 minutes after you have an owner, admin, or manager role (estimate)
verdict.approval_wait: Not documented by Klaviyo. Plan for at least one round of review feedback.

gates.name: Own account (app created, not listed)
gates.unlocks: Create the app, connect and test with your own Klaviyo account. Only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps.
limits: Only owner, admin, or manager roles can create apps
Client secret cannot be viewed again after you save it; it can be regenerated
Authorization codes expire after about 5 minutes

gates.name: Unlisted installation URL (invited customers and testers)
gates.unlocks: Share your installation URL with customers and testers without listing the app. They can install and use it.
limits: Users see an OAuth install warning that the app has not been reviewed by Klaviyo
No user or install cap was found in the sources
Tokens are scoped per Klaviyo account; each merchant account installs separately
Each installed app instance gets its own rate limit quota
gates.time_to_reach: As soon as the Gate 1 flow works end to end and the install URL starts OAuth directly

gates.name: Klaviyo marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Listing in the Klaviyo marketplace, so any Klaviyo user can find and install the app.
limits: Requires at least 5 installs with demonstrated Production-level API activity from real customer accounts
Developer, company, and test accounts do not count
Klaviyo may decline to list any app for any reason
Private API keys are not allowed; apps still on API keys are delisted
Branded metric names cannot be changed after approval
gates.time_to_reach: Not documented; depends on 5 real customer installs, the security assessment, and review feedback

steps.title: Confirm your Klaviyo role
steps.detail: Check that your Klaviyo account has the owner, admin, or manager role. Other roles cannot create OAuth apps.

steps.title: Open Manage apps and create the app
steps.detail: Log in to Klaviyo and go to Integrations > Developers > Manage apps (klaviyo.com/manage-apps). Click Create app and enter a name.
gotchas: Manage apps redirects to a login page if you are not logged in.

steps.title: Enter the redirect URL
steps.detail: Open the app and set its redirect URLs. Paste the Composio callback URL from your Composio auth config. Separate multiple URLs with a space, tab, or newline. These are the only URLs Klaviyo will redirect to after authorization.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The sources disagree on the Composio callback path (v1 auth-apps/add vs v3 toolkits/auth/callback). Confirm it in Composio before saving.

steps.title: Set the scopes to the minimum your integration uses
steps.detail: Enter scopes as a space-separated list. Keep accounts:read, which is required. Add only the scopes your integration actually calls. Do not paste Composio's full default list, because unused scopes get the app rejected.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: accounts:read plus only the scopes your integration calls (space-separated)

gotchas: Testing with Postman needs events:read and events:write.
Reviewers check each scope against the endpoints you list in the testing instructions.

steps.title: Save and copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Save the app. Copy the client ID and client secret immediately. The secret cannot be viewed again; if you lose it, regenerate it and update Composio.
gotchas: Save the secret in a secrets manager at once.

steps.title: Enter the Klaviyo credentials in Composio
steps.detail: In your Composio auth config for the klaviyo toolkit, choose your own OAuth app (not managed auth). Enter the client ID, client secret, and the scope list you trimmed in the previous step.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list is broader than what you need. Replace it.

steps.title: Verify the PKCE and token exchange
steps.detail: Check that the authorization request includes a PKCE code challenge using S256 and a state value that changes per user. Check that the token exchange sends client credentials as Basic auth, uses a form-encoded body, and includes the code verifier and grant_type authorization_code.
gotchas: Community guides may predate the current OAuth 2.1 requirement. Use the official docs as the reference.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Open the installation URL and approve the app with your own Klaviyo account. Finish the authorization within about 5 minutes of the code being issued. Confirm that the access and refresh tokens are stored and that the refresh token is replaced with the new one after each refresh.
gotchas: An install attempted after the authorization code expires fails with a session-invalid error.
Refresh tokens rotate on every use. Storing an old refresh token will break the connection on the next refresh.

steps.title: Build disconnect, denial, and uninstall handling
steps.detail: Add a disconnect action that revokes the user's refresh token. Handle the case where the user denies authorization. Handle uninstall from Klaviyo so the app reflects it. Remove any remaining API-key connection.
gotchas: Common review failures include no disconnect UI and no handling of denial.

steps.title: Test the installation URL from klaviyo.com and a subdomain
steps.detail: Install the app from klaviyo.com and from a klaviyo.com subdomain. Confirm that the installation URL starts OAuth directly and does not redirect to a website first. Also confirm that installing from the Klaviyo listing works without redirects elsewhere.
gotchas: An install URL that redirects to a website instead of starting OAuth is a common review failure.

steps.title: Share the installation URL with test customers
steps.detail: Give your installation URL to invited customers and testers. They will see an unreviewed-app warning but can install and use the app. Use real customer accounts where you can, because test accounts do not count toward listing.
gotchas: No user or install cap was found in the sources. Confirm limits in Klaviyo before you invite a large group.

steps.title: Draft the listing and testing instructions
steps.detail: Draft 2-6 key features (titles up to 65 characters, descriptions up to 225). Draft 1-4 linked articles including one user guide (titles up to 100 characters). Set a settings URL that points to a Klaviyo-specific integration settings page. Draft testing instructions that list each scope with the endpoints it covers and the use case.
gotchas: Scopes that do not match the submission cause failure.

steps.title: Collect 5 real customer installs with live API activity
steps.detail: Get at least 5 installs from real customer accounts that make live API calls at Production level. Developer, company, and test accounts do not count.
gotchas: Installs are gathered by sharing the installation URL.

steps.title: Complete the security assessment and submit
steps.detail: Complete the security assessment form and the registration forms. Confirm the OAuth setup and link the testing instructions. Then go to Integrations > Developers > Manage apps, click your app name, and click Review submission.
gotchas: Address feedback from the Security and Trust team before resubmitting.

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: Klaviyo reviews the submission and may decline to list it for any reason. Plan for at least one round of feedback. After approval, app metrics use your logo and branded metric names cannot be changed.
gotchas: No review turnaround time was found in Klaviyo's pages.

requirements.item: Owner, admin, or manager role to create the app
requirements.detail: Only these roles can create OAuth apps in Klaviyo.

requirements.item: PKCE with S256 on the authorization request
requirements.detail: Klaviyo requires PKCE and uses OAuth 2.1. Composio's flow must send a code challenge.
Request only the scopes your integration calls. Apps requesting more scopes than necessary are rejected.
accounts:read is required by default and must stay in the list.

requirements.item: Installation URL kicks off OAuth directly
requirements.detail: The install URL must start OAuth with code challenge and per-user state, not redirect to a website.

requirements.item: Installable from klaviyo.com and its subdomains
requirements.detail: Apps with an install flow only on their own platform are rejected.
Apps must revoke the refresh token on disconnect, handle denial and errors, and reflect uninstall from Klaviyo.
Apps still on private API keys are delisted and cannot be listed.
Real customer accounts only; developer, company, and test accounts do not count.
Complete the form and address feedback from the Security and Trust team.

requirements.item: Listing content: 2-6 key features and 1-4 linked articles including a user guide
requirements.detail: Feature titles up to 65 characters, descriptions up to 225; article titles up to 100 characters.
The settings URL must point to a Klaviyo-specific integration settings page for the app.

scopes.effect: Required by default and must remain in the list.
Needed for Postman testing. Include them only if your integration or testing uses them, since unused scopes get the app flagged.
Too broad for Klaviyo's least-permissive rule. Trim to the endpoints your integration calls before submitting. Reviewers flag unused scopes.

blockers.symptom: App is delisted or cannot be listed while it still uses a private API key connection.
blockers.cause: Klaviyo allows only OAuth apps in its listing. Private-key (API key) connections are not allowed.
blockers.fix: Migrate every customer connection to OAuth and remove API-key connections before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Listing submission cannot proceed; the app does not meet the install requirement.
blockers.cause: Klaviyo requires at least 5 installs with live Production-level API activity from real customer accounts. Test, developer, and company accounts do not count.
blockers.fix: Share the installation URL with real customers, and wait until 5 accounts show live API activity before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Review rejects the app for requesting more scopes than necessary.
blockers.cause: The scope list is copied from Composio's default, which is broader than the endpoints the integration calls.
blockers.fix: Trim the scope list to the endpoints you call, and list each scope with its endpoints in the testing instructions.

blockers.symptom: Review fails on the install flow: the installation URL redirects to a website.
blockers.cause: The installation URL does not start OAuth directly, or install does not work from klaviyo.com subdomains.
blockers.fix: Make the installation URL begin the OAuth flow with a code challenge and per-user state. Test installs from klaviyo.com and a subdomain.

blockers.symptom: Submission is held on the security assessment.
blockers.cause: The security assessment form is incomplete, or Security and Trust feedback is not yet addressed.
blockers.fix: Complete the security assessment form and resolve each item of Security and Trust feedback before resubmitting.

composio.note: Composio's managed OAuth app is not available for Klaviyo, so you must register your own Klaviyo OAuth app and enter its client ID and client secret in Composio. Do not keep Composio's default scope list: Klaviyo expects the least permissive scope set, so request only the scopes your integration calls. Authorize URL: https://www.klaviyo.com/oauth/authorize. Token URL: https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token. Confirm the exact Composio callback URL in Composio's own setup before you register it, because the sources disagree on the path.

open_questions: Refresh-token lifetime and expiry are not documented; only the 1-hour access token and rotation on each use were found.
No review turnaround time was found in Klaviyo's pages.
No user or install cap for unlisted installs was found. Confirm before inviting a large group.
No account prerequisites were documented beyond the owner, admin, or manager role: no paid plan, partner program, business verification, or review fee.
Whether the listing review requires domain verification, specific logo sizes, or a demo video was not found.
The Composio callback URL to allowlist is inconsistent between the toolkit record (v1 auth-apps/add) and the probe (v3 path). Confirm it in Composio before registering.
Client ID validation at the Klaviyo authorize endpoint could not be observed, because the probe redirected to a login page.
The Klaviyo docs fetched were version v2023-10-15 and related pages; some community guides may be outdated.
